summary: Radar for 2026-10-21, GLP-1 focus. The strongest opening is still the gray-market lane (Lane B). CBS News published its own lab tests of products sold as "retatrutide" on Oct 21. The two online samples matched only a basic reference standard, not Lilly's trial drug, and the corner-store vial didn't appear to contain a peptide at all. Behind that come the 22-lot compounded tirzepatide recall, now classified Class II (headlines are wrongly tying it to Mounjaro and Zepbound), and a USA Today "is your online pharmacy legit?" piece. Lane A search-question long-forms have three timely hooks: Thanksgiving and holiday eating (peaks in about 4–5 weeks, ideal lead time), a new AAO 2026 analysis showing the apparent macular degeneration risk was driven by cardiometabolic conditions rather than the drug, and menopause plus semaglutide. Fresh but low-confidence items are labelled caution: the semaglutide crime trial reported in BMJ, sperm health, cannabis and the immune system. Verification notes: (1) The tirzepatide heart-risk label was approved on Aug 28, 2026, so it isn't Lane C news. (2) The Zepbound KwikPen approval is from early 2026, so it's old. (3) The menopause hormone therapy data people are citing traces back to a small 2024 Mayo cohort (16 women on hormone therapy vs 90 without), so it needs careful wording. (4) The 20 attorneys general letter seems to be from September and only reported now. (5) Scheduling check: the CBS retatrutide and recall topics touch Shorts published in the last 14 days, so a long-form must lead with the new fact (lab tests, Class II meaning) and the scheduler must confirm the 14-day rule. No compounded or switching how-to content was proposed. The earlier rejects still stand.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide sold online: what CBS News' lab tests found (Oct 21, 2026), and what the FDA and Lilly have confirmed
candidates.angle: Lane B long-form 'Retatrutide Online: What Lab Tests and the FDA Confirmed'. Calm, sourced line by line, with every line dated: (1) CBS bought 3 products sold as retatrutide; a University of Iowa scientist found the 2 online samples matched only a basic reference standard, not Lilly's trial drug, and the corner-store vial appeared to have no peptide at all. (2) It is not approved anywhere; Lilly plans to file in Q1 2027. (3) Deaths reported to FDA are unverified reports. Never name sellers. Point viewers to a prescriber about approved options or trials. New fact compared with our earlier bootleg Short: the lab results.
candidates.why_now: The CBS investigation went live Oct 21 and was syndicated to Yahoo and Newser. It stacks on the Oct 19 Partnership for Safe Medicines death report, the Penn Reddit AI study, illegal retatrutide rising in the Netherlands, and Australian ED admissions. 'Retatrutide online' searches keep climbing, and this is our strongest lane (Short median 102).

evidence.signal: Lab-tested 3 'retatrutide' products; online samples matched only a basic standard, not Lilly's drug; bodega vial had no apparent peptide

Use for Shorts; a long-form only if it's clearly differentiated and passes the 14-day check.
